turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag, sorry, parking was a whole mission. I'm his mum, and this is Grace, she stays with us and helps with the baby. He's ten days old today.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're welcome, no rush. What's been worrying you?

[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's his colour, hey. His skin's gone yellow, the face and down over the chest, and the whites of his eyes look yellow too. I noticed it from about day three, so it's been about a week, and in hospital they did a blood test and they said it was borderline so they sent us home. I still second-guess it under the warm passage bulb, so I check him at the window, sometimes more than once.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the feeding, in your own words.

[SEG0005] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, breast milk both sides, he latches okay most feeds though he slips off and fusses now and then. Then we top up with formula every four hours, day and night. Last night he went five hours once and I just about woke him, then he drank fine. Wet nappies are six or seven a day, and the stools are that yellow seedy kind, not pale.
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I make the bottles. It's about forty mils of NAN, though he often stops around thirty. Breast first, then the bottle, every four hours.
[SEG0007] person_4 (PATIENT): Mm.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has he had any fever?

[SEG0009] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Umm. Last night his neck felt a bit warm, but the room was stuffy and I never found the thermometer, and this morning he feels like himself. So I don't actually think it was a fever, maybe it was nothing. I do spiral a bit, sorry.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any cough, or is his breathing noisy or fast?
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. No cough. Breathing is quiet, just normal baby breaths. I've sat and watched.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): And vomiting? Or a runny tummy?
[SEG0013] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, not once. Stools aren't loose either. Three yesterday, I counted them, sorry, I count when I'm nervous.
[SEG0014] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sister weighed him just now. Three point three eight kilograms. He was three point one when he was born, so he's picked up a little.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Let me have a look at him.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja, he is yellow in the face and on the chest, and the whites of the eyes are yellow too. He's alert, his tummy is soft, and he's not in distress.
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): Ah.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're breastfeeding, so what medicines are you taking yourself?

[SEG0019] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yoh, quite a list, I always over-explain. I'm on amlodopine for the pressure, um five milligrams, no sorry, it's ten milligrams in the morning. The cholesterol one at night is atorvastaten twenty milligrams for the cholesterol, and my sugar tablets are metformin five hundred milligrams twice a day for the sugar. Only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning as well, from the health shop, maybe a teaspoon, I don't really measure it.

[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the iron, ferrous sulphate two hundred milligrams, I stopped it in March because it was upsetting my stomach. They said I could take aspirin after I had him, but I never took that, not one tablet.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's been sleepier on the breast today. I have to tickle his feet or he dozes off.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. My working impression is ordinary newborn jaundice, though it could still be the breast-milk kind. I don't want to decide which until we see the level.

[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like a bilirubin blood test today, before you go. Keep feeding every four hours, breast then the formula, and wake him if he goes longer than that. I'd leave that powder for now, just till we know what's going on.
[SEG0024] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Today, ja, alright. If the powder is a problem I'll leave it. It's just a shop mix, turmeric or something, I think. I do go on, sorry.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back tomorrow and we'll go through the result together.
[SEG0026] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if he gets more yellow tonight, or he won't wake for a feed, I shouldn't wait for tomorrow, hey?
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's right. If he gets more yellow, or he won't wake to feed, come straight back. Don't sit on it.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll set an alarm for the feeds. The clinic card is on the kitchen counter, the sister wrote on it.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bring the card if you remember, but it's fine if it's still on the counter. You're both doing a good job.
[SEG0030] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Shame, thank you. I'll try not to google all night. Three point one at birth and three point three eight today still feels small to me, but anyway.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's a fair gain for ten days. We'll see you tomorrow.

spec.situation: Parents with a ten-day-old baby, yellow skin and feeding every four hours; weight read by the nurse; breast milk plus formula; blood test for bilirubin planned today.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Caregiver reports sleepier today; exact duration '1 day' not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Sleepiness (category=neurological, status=present, duration=1 day, temporality=current, reported_by=caregiver, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Current morning Ayurvedic powder supported; exact dose 1 teaspoon is only an estimate.
bad.text: Ayurvedic powder (dose=1 teaspoon, frequency=once daily, status=currently_used, reported_by=family_member)

bad.reason: Earlier hospital blood test mentioned, but bilirubin and completed status aren't stated.
bad.text: Bilirubin blood test (type=laboratory, status=completed, indication=Reported as borderline)

omissions.text: Fever was specifically asked about and effectively denied: mother said his neck felt warm last night but she did not measure a temperature and does not think it was a fever; this morning he seems like himself.
Feeding detail not captured: breastfeeding both sides, latches okay most feeds but sometimes slips off and fusses.

Feeding schedule/detail not fully captured: formula top-up is specifically NAN, about 40 mL though he often only takes around 30 mL, given after breastfeeding every 4 hours day and night; one overnight interval stretched to 5 hours once and mother woke him, after which he fed fine.
Hydration/output details missing: wet nappies are 6 to 7 per day.
Stool detail missing: stools are yellow and seedy, not pale; there were three stools yesterday.

Previous investigation detail is incomplete/wrongly represented: in hospital they did a blood test when jaundice was first noticed and said it was 'borderline' before discharging him home; the recorded fact labels this as a completed bilirubin blood test but does not reflect that this was historical information from hospital rather than a test completed in this encounter.
Birth weight was stated as 3.1 kg.
Sleepiness detail not fully captured: caregiver said he has been sleepier specifically on the breast today and needs foot-tickling to stay awake.
Medication timing detail missing for amlodipine: 10 mg in the morning.
Ayurvedic powder contents were partly described as a shop mix, 'turmeric or something'.
Aspirin history missing: she was told she could take aspirin after delivery but she never took any, not one tablet.
